public_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Track in-place subject edits after resolving an alias**

After an alias has been resolved once, removing the target from `model_fields_set` prevents subsequent in-place edits from being detected: `references_set_in_code()` returns `False` before comparing reference IDs. For example, save a dashboard with `roles = [5]`, then call `dashboard.viewers.append(subject_id)`, assign `dashboard.roles = [6]`, and save again; the explicitly appended subject is silently dropped. Unlike the previously reported direct-assignment case, the fresh evidence here is that alias resolution itself removes the bookkeeping needed to recognize later list mutations. Record the resolved list as a new baseline while still allowing subsequent in-place changes to count as explicit subject edits.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
